title: Power Rankings: Celtics slipping, Jazz surging
heading: 2009-10 Power Rankings: Week 14
author: Marc Stein

rankings.summaryHtml: With so much momentum and such a helpful schedule -- Cleveland has just 14 road games left -- methinks we can safely say Mo Williams got hurt at the right time. Only Denver matched the Cavs' 12-3 record in January.

rankings.summaryHtml: Kobe shot 41.3 percent from the floor in January with that mangled index finger, but I'm guessing we remember his final shot Jan. 31 in Boston if anything from the first month of the new decade sticks in the memory.

rankings.summaryHtml: Q: Who has the league's best record against teams at .500 or better? A: Denver at 21-8. Easier one: Who should fill CP3's All-Star spot? Answer: Denver is 6-3 when Melo is out, which only strengthens Chauncey's case.

rankings.summaryHtml: Boston's failing health and Orlando's spell over Atlanta suggest that the Magic will reach the All-Star break as the closest thing to a co-favorite in the East with Cleveland. Even with fresh injuries for Jameer and Pietrus.

rankings.summaryHtml: So many good things cooking. With the game in his home state of Texas, D-Will is finally an All-Star. Utah just posted the NBA's fourth-best January record at 10-4. And it all seemed to start when Sundiata Gaines showed up.

rankings.summaryHtml: What tells you more? The Hawks' three wins in January over the Celtics that clinched a 4-0 season sweep? Or the follow-up loss in Orlando that dropped Atlanta to 0-3 against the Magic ... by a combined 67 points?

rankings.summaryHtml: For a group frequently tagged as soft, this is momentous: Toronto just became the first team since November 2002 to trail by at least 10 points in four straight games and win all four. Foes: Knicks, Heat, Lakers and Bucks.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Mavs know what's wrong. They're just not sure how to fix it, because they've been talking about the same problems -- insufficient focus at home and a slip from the top five to 11th in defensive efficiency -- for weeks.

rankings.summaryHtml: I repeat: G-Wallace is an undeniable All-Star, but why is nobody is talking about S-Jax? Jack's partnership with Wallace just sparked the Bobs to 12 wins in January alone. Previous team record for one month? Nine.

rankings.summaryHtml: The schedule, with consecutive games against the Magic, Hawks and Lakers, wasn't exactly soft. But alarm bells are going to ring loudly when the Celts, no matter what injury alibis they have, go 6-11 after a 23-5 start.

rankings.summaryHtml: Not that we'd ever suggest Andre Miller's 52-point eruption Saturday night in Dallas -- with B-Roy sidelined -- was unexpected ... but you do know Dre scored a whopping two points the previous night in Houston. Right?

rankings.summaryHtml: Conversation that I never expected to have in January of the 2009-10 season: Prominent NBA player stops me in my tracks Saturday night to ask if I can believe that the Griz just lost at home to the CP3-less Hornets.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Bulls have taken loads of flak for their Circus Road Trip ineptitude since MJ retired, but they just got some historic revenge by becoming the first team ever to win five straight roadies against teams with winning records.
rankings.summaryText: The Bulls have taken loads of flak for their Circus Road Trip ineptitude since MJ retired, but they just got some historic revenge by becoming the first team ever to win five straight roadies against teams with winning records.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Rodeo Road Trip can't turn the Spurs around like it usually does if the Tony Parker ankle injury that sucked so much joy out of those much-needed wins over Atlanta and Memphis forces him to miss most of the trip.

rankings.summaryHtml: Even after pulling out big wins in close games against two quality Western Conference rivals -- Dallas and Houston -- Phoenix is probably right where it should be with this small, thin roster. Scuffling for a playoff spot.

rankings.summaryHtml: January was only Durant's best month as a pro. He averaged 32.1 points for the month and signed off with his fourth 40-point game of the season, placing him fourth in the league behind Kobe (7), Melo (5) and LeBron (5).

rankings.summaryHtml: The Hornets had won 11 straight overtime games at home, dating all the way to March 2005 when they were playing in OKC, before Friday's disastrous OT loss to Chicago, during which they lost the streak and CP3.

rankings.summaryHtml: More evidence that relying so much on scrappiness is gradually taking its toll: Houston is 1-4 on this six-game homestand to fall to 14-9 at the Toyota Center. Last season? The Rockets lost eight home games total.

rankings.summaryHtml: The good news: Miami still hasn't spent a single day this season below .500. The bad news: There are suddenly eight teams with winning records in everyone's favorite punching-bag conference. And the D-Wades are No. 8.

rankings.summaryHtml: A 3-10 record in games decided by three points or less is tough to take in any circumstance ... but it really leaves the East's No. 9 team with a sense of regret now that Toronto, Charlotte and Chicago have all gotten so hot.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Clips have two stops left on an eight-game road trip and are 1-5 on the junket after losses at (gulp) New Jersey and Minnesota. So you tell me: Are we down to 11 teams playing for eight playoff berths in the West?
